editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the depolarizing-channel explanation (« avec une probabilité $p$, l'état est remplacé par l'état complètement mixte, et l'état est préservé avec une probabilité $1 - p$ »), the 2 % CX error, the $(1-p)^m$ decay and the 65 % « estimation conservatrice … ne tient pas compte de l'état initial » all match the English exactly; no drift, no hallucination, and « tu » is held consistently. Core terms are correct and stable (qubit, porte CX, observable, valeur d'espérance, modèle de bruit, primitive Estimator/Sampler). Two purely stylistic calques a native technical editor would change: « des erreurs, ou bruits » pluralizes what is a mass noun in French (« ou du bruit »), and « échantillonner depuis le circuit bruité » is an English-shaped construction (natives write « échantillonner le circuit bruité » or « à partir du circuit bruité »). Neither misleads.

examples.source: Currently existing quantum processors suffer from errors, or noise, so the results of an exact simulation…
examples.suggested: …sont sujets à des erreurs, ou du bruit, de sorte que…
examples.translation: Les processeurs quantiques actuels sont sujets à des erreurs, ou bruits, de sorte que les résultats d'une simulation exacte…
examples.why: « bruit » is a mass noun in French technical usage; the plural « bruits » reads as a literal echo of the English apposition and is not how a French quantum engineer would write it. Meaning is unaffected.

examples.source: …how to use the Sampler primitive from Qiskit Aer to sample from the noisy circuit.
examples.suggested: …pour échantillonner le circuit bruité (ou : à partir du circuit bruité).
examples.translation: …comment utiliser la primitive Sampler de Qiskit Aer pour échantillonner depuis le circuit bruité.
examples.why: « échantillonner depuis X » calques the English "sample from"; in French the verb takes a direct object, or « à partir de » if a source must be marked. Stiff but unambiguous.

examples.source: …do not necessarily reflect the results you would expect when running circuits on real hardware.
examples.suggested: …ne reflètent pas nécessairement les résultats auxquels tu t'attendrais en exécutant les circuits sur du matériel réel.
examples.translation: …ne reflètent pas nécessairement ce que tu obtiendrais en exécutant les circuits sur du matériel réel.
examples.why: « ce que tu obtiendrais » drops the "expect" nuance (what you would actually get vs. what you would anticipate). Very slight flattening of the pedagogical point; not misleading, since the surrounding sentence still contrasts simulation with hardware.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the hard parts (Arnoldi orthogonalisation, the steepest-descent motivation, the generalized eigenvalue problem $\tilde H\vec c = E\tilde S\vec c$, the efficient Hadamard test, and the whole Appendix I error bound) all say exactly what the English says, and the informal "tu" register holds consistently ("Rappelle-toi", "N'hésite pas", "Tu peux jouer"). The defects are editorial, not misleading. (1) At l.196 the English "this is intended to help us solve eigenvalue problems of extremely large matrices" (referring to the Krylov *method*) becomes "cet exemple est destiné à nous aider à résoudre…", which attributes to the 3×3 toy example a purpose the same paragraph has just denied it. (2) "Hamiltonian" is split by casing across the file: capitalised "Hamiltonien" throughout §3–§4.1 (l.699, 741, 760, 902, 944, 974) but lowercase "hamiltonien" — the correct French form — in §1 and from §4.2 onward (l.315, 1129, 1664, 1673, 1783); a two-pass-merge signature. (3) "scaling" is rendered three ways: the calque "mise à l'échelle" (heading l.531 "Mise à l'échelle temporelle selon la dimension de la matrice"; l.385, 1660, 1666), "évolue comme / l'évolution dominante" (l.697), where a native writer would say "comportement asymptotique" or "évolution du temps de calcul". Smaller slips: the acronym is introduced as "DQK" (l.4, l.15) then never reused, with the English "KQD" appearing undefined at l.534/1673/1675; "le primitif Estimator" (l.750, wrong gender/word) vs the correct "une primitive Qiskit Runtime" (l.1313); the typo "Nous transpilon" (l.1284); "état vide" for "vacuum state" (l.1130, should be "état du vide"); "creusité" (l.691) vs "sparsité" (l.315) / "matrices creuses" (l.385); and "motivate"/"argue" both flattened to "montrer" at l.313 while l.385 correctly uses "motiver".

examples.source: Indeed, as we will see in later sections, the Krylov method is only advantageous above a certain matrix dimension; this is intended to help us solve eigenvalue/eigenvector problems of extremely large matrices.
examples.suggested: … ; la méthode est destinée à nous aider à résoudre des problèmes aux valeurs propres/vecteurs propres de matrices extrêmement grandes.
examples.translation: En effet, comme nous le verrons dans les sections suivantes, la méthode de Krylov n'est avantageuse qu'à partir d'une certaine dimension de matrice ; cet exemple est destiné à nous aider à résoudre des problèmes aux valeurs propres/vecteurs propres pour des matrices extrêmement grandes.
examples.why: The English "this" refers to the Krylov method; the French pins it on "cet exemple", i.e. the 3×3 toy matrix the same paragraph has just said shows no advantage. The main claim survives, but the referent slip contradicts the surrounding setup.

examples.source: Hamiltonian
examples.suggested: Use lowercase "hamiltonien" everywhere (standard French for a common noun derived from a proper name).
examples.why: Same term rendered two ways within one file, split cleanly by section, which is the fingerprint of two merged translation passes. Not misleading, but a native editor would unify it.

examples.source: ### 2.2 Time scaling with matrix dimension … we have made no numerical claims about the scaling of this approach
examples.suggested: ### 2.2 Évolution du temps de calcul avec la dimension de la matrice … aucune affirmation numérique sur le comportement asymptotique (la complexité) de cette approche
examples.translation: ### 2.2 Mise à l'échelle temporelle selon la dimension de la matrice … nous n'avons fait aucune affirmation numérique sur la mise à l'échelle de cette approche
examples.why: "Mise à l'échelle" means scaling *up* / rescaling, not asymptotic complexity; as a heading "Mise à l'échelle temporelle" reads like "temporal upscaling". The file elsewhere uses "évolue comme" (l.697) for the same idea, so the calque is both stiff and inconsistent.

examples.source: Krylov quantum diagonalization (KQD) … not the ideal application for KQD
examples.suggested: Pick one: either define "(DQK)" and use DQK throughout, or keep "(KQD)" in the intro to match the later body text.
examples.translation: la diagonalisation quantique de Krylov (DQK) … pas l'application idéale pour KQD
examples.why: The lesson teaches the acronym DQK in the intro and frontmatter, then uses the undefined English acronym KQD in §2.2 and §5. The concept stays identifiable, but the learner is handed an abbreviation that never reappears.

examples.source: can be realized using the Qiskit Runtime primitive Estimator … Step 3. Execute using a Qiskit Runtime primitive
examples.suggested: … à l'aide de la primitive Estimator de Qiskit Runtime
examples.translation: peuvent être réalisées à l'aide du primitif Estimator de Qiskit Runtime … Étape 3. Exécuter avec une primitive Qiskit Runtime
examples.why: "Primitive" is feminine in French and is correctly rendered "une primitive" in the §4.3 heading; "le primitif" at l.750 is both the wrong gender and a different noun, inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: Overall faithful and readable, with correct, consistent core terminology ("valore di aspettazione", "soppressione degli errori", "shot", "primitiva Sampler/Estimator", "la moda" for statistical mode) and a consistent informal "tu" register. Two content-level slips: in the Description section "so you can easily swap in the Q-CTRL Sampler and Estimator" became "così puoi facilmente sostituire Q-CTRL Sampler ed Estimator", which in Italian reads as replacing the Q-CTRL primitives rather than swapping them in for the standard ones (the correct direction is stated correctly earlier at line 48, "usarla al posto delle primitive Qiskit Runtime standard"); and the 2026-02-20 changelog entry silently drops the second English sentence telling users the job ID is still reachable via the runtime service's `job_id()` method, leaving a deprecation notice with no migration path. Lexically, English "consistent" is calqued twice as the false friend "consistente" ("accuratezza ... estremamente consistente", "rimanere consistente"), where Italian wants "costante"/"coerente"; "accuracy" alternates between "precisione" (line 44) and "accuratezza" (lines 76, 78, 86); and "la necessità di costosi post-processing" mismatches number/gender (should be "del costoso post-processing").

examples.source: Fire Opal Performance Management has two options for execution that are similar to the Qiskit Runtime primitives, so you can easily swap in the Q-CTRL Sampler and Estimator.
examples.suggested: ... così puoi facilmente sostituire le primitive standard con il Sampler e l'Estimator di Q-CTRL.
examples.translation: Fire Opal Performance Management offre due opzioni di esecuzione simili alle primitive Qiskit Runtime, così puoi facilmente sostituire Q-CTRL Sampler ed Estimator.
examples.why: Bare 'sostituire X' in Italian means 'replace X', inverting the direction of the substitution: the reader is told the Q-CTRL primitives are what gets replaced, whereas the English says they are what you drop in. Contradicts the correct rendering already used at line 48.

examples.source: - 2026-02-20: Deprecation Notice - the `provider_job_ids` metadata field will be deprecated in 30 days in version 0.13.0. Users can access the job ID through `job_id()` method of the runtime service.
examples.suggested: ... nella versione 0.13.0. Gli utenti possono accedere all'ID del job tramite il metodo `job_id()` del runtime service.
examples.translation: - 2026-02-20: Avviso di deprecazione — il campo di metadati `provider_job_ids` verrà deprecato tra 30 giorni nella versione 0.13.0.
examples.why: The entire second sentence — the replacement API for the deprecated field — is missing, so the Italian reader gets the deprecation without the migration path.

examples.source: extremely consistent solution accuracy / the value of $A$ should remain consistent
examples.suggested: un'accuratezza della soluzione estremamente costante / il valore di $A$ dovrebbe rimanere costante (o 'coerente')
examples.translation: un'accuratezza della soluzione estremamente consistente / il valore di $A$ dovrebbe rimanere consistente
examples.why: 'consistente' is a false friend: in Italian it means substantial/solid, not 'unvarying'. A native technical writer would use 'costante' or 'coerente'.

examples.source: increased accuracy enabled by Performance Management ... Accuracy ... Measure of accuracy
examples.suggested: la maggiore accuratezza abilitata da Performance Management
examples.translation: la maggiore precisione abilitata da Performance Management ... Accuratezza ... Misura dell'accuratezza
examples.why: 'accuracy' is rendered as 'precisione' in the Overview but as 'accuratezza' in the Benchmarks prose, table headers and metric definition; in measurement contexts precisione/accuratezza are distinct concepts, so the split is worth unifying on 'accuratezza'.

examples.source: By preventing errors, the need for expensive post-processing is eliminated.
examples.suggested: Prevenendo gli errori, si elimina la necessità di un costoso post-processing.
examples.translation: Prevenendo gli errori, si elimina la necessità di costosi post-processing.
examples.why: 'post-processing' is treated as an uncountable masculine singular in Italian; the plural adjective 'costosi' does not agree and reads as an unedited MT artifact.

editor_note: Terminology and register are solid and consistent throughout: job/batch/session/QPU/drift/ansatz/wall-clock time are kept in English as the field does, "osservabile", "mitigazione degli errori", "modello di rumore" and "funzione di costo" are the conventional renderings, and the informal "tu" holds everywhere ("utilizza", "consulta", "dovresti", "a meno che tu non abbia"). One real but non-misleading drift: in the variational-algorithm example the English "It could also take longer to converge due to device drift" becomes "Potrebbe anche richiedere più iterazioni per convergere" — time-to-converge is silently converted into a count of iterations, a claim the source does not make (though it stays consistent with the next sentence about drift worsening subsequent results). Secondary style slip: "dovresti ottimizzare il tuo carico di lavoro per trovare il rapporto ottimale" repeats the ottimizzare/ottimale root where the English has "tune ... optimal ratio"; a native technical writer would write "regolare/tarare il carico di lavoro". Neither would teach a learner anything false.

examples.source: It could also take longer to converge due to device drift.
examples.suggested: Potrebbe anche richiedere più tempo per convergere a causa del drift del dispositivo.
examples.translation: Potrebbe anche richiedere più iterazioni per convergere a causa del drift del dispositivo.
examples.why: The English claims a longer convergence time (the whole paragraph is about wall-clock time inflated by queuing); the Italian substitutes a different quantity — number of iterations — which the source never asserts. Plausible but not what the English teaches.

examples.source: you should tune your workload to find the optimal ratio
examples.suggested: dovresti regolare (o tarare) il tuo carico di lavoro per trovare il rapporto ottimale
examples.translation: dovresti ottimizzare il tuo carico di lavoro per trovare il rapporto ottimale
examples.why: 'ottimizzare ... ottimale' repeats the same root in one clause, and 'ottimizzare' overshoots 'tune' (which here means adjusting parameters, not optimizing). A native technical writer would use 'regolare' or 'tarare'.

editor_note: The file is a pure bibliography (136 IEEE-style entries) whose only translatable prose is the title, description and one heading; all three are rendered idiomatically ("Works cited" → "Opere citate", "Full list of references" → "Elenco completo dei riferimenti", description → "Questo documento fornisce un elenco di tutte le citazioni utilizzate nel corso."), and the 136 citation entries are correctly left untranslated in English with authors, volumes, page ranges, dates and DOIs matching the source one-for-one (spot-checked [39] "20 million noisy qubits", [40] "177 Days with 13 436 Qubits", [103] pp. 2–17 Jan. 1987). No drift, no hallucination, nothing an Italian technical editor would change.

Meaning is faithful throughout — the QPY forward-compatibility caveat ("saranno compatibili con le versioni più recenti di Qiskit (ma non necessariamente con le versioni precedenti)") preserves both direction and hedge, and the informal "tu" register holds consistently (Usa / Puoi / se riavvii il kernel Python). The one defect is a grammatical number slip repeated twice: "una lista di circuito" (singular) instead of "una lista di circuiti", at line 49 ("Puoi anche salvare una lista di circuito") and line 58 ("restituisce sempre una lista di circuito, anche se ne hai serializzato uno solo"). It does not mislead — the following clause "anche se ne hai serializzato uno solo" makes the plural sense recoverable — but a native editor would fix it, since the whole point of the sentence is that the return value is a list of multiple circuits. Terminology otherwise correct and consistent (circuito quantistico, serializzazione QPY, kernel Python, serializzare).

examples.source: You can also save a list of circuits.
examples.suggested: Puoi anche salvare una lista di circuiti.
examples.translation: Puoi anche salvare una lista di circuito.
examples.why: Plural agreement error: 'lista di circuito' is ungrammatical and blunts the point that dump accepts multiple circuits.

examples.source: Note that this always returns a list of circuits, even if you only serialized one circuit.
examples.suggested: Nota che questa funzione restituisce sempre una lista di circuiti, anche se ne hai serializzato uno solo.
examples.translation: Nota che questa funzione restituisce sempre una lista di circuito, anche se ne hai serializzato uno solo.
examples.why: Same singular/plural slip; here the contrast with 'uno solo' makes the missing plural especially jarring for a native reader.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every quantity (depth 251 / two-qubit 165, "più di 100 anche prima della traspilazione", 0,90^10 ≈ 35%, primi 90 punti per l'addestramento e i successivi 30 per il test, dimensione dettata dai punti di addestramento non dalle caratteristiche) and every caveat (quasi-probabilità, diagonale posta a 1 in assenza di rumore, "molto diverso dal vantaggio quantistico") survives intact. The real defect is a repeated singular/plural agreement corruption of "circuito": "Per circuito complicati" (l.174), "produceva circuito piuttosto profondi" (l.621), and three in one paragraph at l.734 ("in circuito molto grandi e complessi", "circuito traspilati diversi", "circuito molto grandi") — a native would never write these. Secondary: "primitive" is rendered as masculine "Primitivi Qiskit Runtime" in the Step-3 headings (ll.63, 189) but correctly feminine "le primitive"/"la primitiva `Sampler`" elsewhere (ll.68, 401, 775), and "gate" flips gender ("la profondità delle gate" l.59, "sulle gate native" l.174 vs "la profondità totale dei gate" l.769). A few calques remain ("prendere il circuito più superficiale" for shallowest, "quando quel tasso di errore viene composto" for compounded, "Il dataset è probabile che tragga beneficio…"). Informal "tu" holds throughout.

examples.source: For complicated circuits, this step will substantially increase the circuit depth … / the zz_feature_map produced rather deep circuits … / in very large, complex circuits the pass manager can return different transpiled circuits each time
examples.suggested: Per circuiti complicati … produceva circuiti piuttosto profondi … in circuiti molto grandi e complessi … può restituire circuiti traspilati diversi
examples.translation: Per circuito complicati, questo passaggio aumenterà sostanzialmente la profondità del circuito … / la `zz_feature_map` produceva circuito piuttosto profondi … / in circuito molto grandi e complessi il pass manager può restituire circuito traspilati diversi a ogni esecuzione
examples.why: Systematic singular/plural agreement failure (looks like a botched find-and-replace of 'circuiti'→'circuito'); five occurrences, all ungrammatical Italian. Meaning is still recoverable, so it does not mislead, but no native technical writer would leave it.

examples.source: Step 3: Execute using Qiskit Runtime Primitives
examples.suggested: Passo 3: Eseguire usando le primitive di Qiskit Runtime (everywhere)
examples.translation: Passo 3: Eseguire usando i Primitivi Qiskit Runtime (ll.63, 189) — but 'Ottimizzare il problema ed eseguire con le primitive' (l.401) and 'Eseguire con le primitive di Qiskit Runtime' (l.775)
examples.why: 'Primitivi' is the wrong gender for the Qiskit domain term, which the same file otherwise renders correctly as feminine 'le primitive' / 'la primitiva `Sampler`'. Within-file inconsistency on a core term.

examples.source: minimize gate depth / maps to native gates / variation in the total gate depth
examples.suggested: Pick one gender: 'dei gate' (masculine, standard in Italian Qiskit usage) throughout, or 'delle porte'.
examples.translation: minimizzare la profondità delle gate … sulle gate native … variazione nella profondità totale dei gate
examples.why: 'gate' flips between feminine and masculine within the file; defensible either way, but not both.

examples.source: It is often useful to transpile a few times and take the shallowest circuit.
examples.suggested: È spesso utile traspilare più volte e prendere il circuito meno profondo.
examples.translation: È spesso utile traspilare più volte e prendere il circuito più superficiale.
examples.why: 'superficiale' is a literal calque of 'shallow' meaning superficial/shallow-in-character, not low-depth; the Review section itself uses the right phrasing ('il circuito con la profondità più bassa', l.832).

examples.source: When that error rate is compounded over many qubits … / Is the dataset likely to benefit from quantum kernel methods?
examples.suggested: Quando quel tasso di errore si accumula su molti qubit … / È probabile che il dataset tragga beneficio dai metodi di quantum kernel?
examples.translation: Quando quel tasso di errore viene composto su molti qubit … / Il dataset è probabile che tragga beneficio dai metodi di quantum kernel?
examples.why: 'viene composto' is a false-friend calque of 'compounded'; the Review bullet has English subject-fronting that Italian syntax does not allow naturally. Both stiff, neither misleading.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every Card description tracks its English source faithfully (ZNE's "estrapolando i risultati del valore di aspettazione rumorosi al limite zero-rumore", OBP's "rimuovendo operazioni dalla sua fine al costo di più misurazioni degli operatori"), the informal "tu" holds ("Scopri", "per aiutarti a scegliere"), and "valore di aspettazione" is used consistently. What a native technical editor would change: (1) "unbiased estimate" is rendered "stima imparziale" — "imparziale" is the fairness sense; the statistical term is "stima non distorta"/"non polarizzata"; (2) "Modello di esecuzione diretto" attaches "diretto" to "modello" rather than to the execution — should be "Modello di esecuzione diretta"; (3) "Noise-tailoring technique" → "Tecnica di adattamento al rumore" flips the direction (the technique shapes the noise, it does not adapt to it), though the following clause repairs the sense; (4) half-translated hybrids "Decoupling dinamico" and "lightcone sfumati" where Italian usage is either full English or "disaccoppiamento dinamico"/"coni di luce". None of these would leave a learner with a false concept.

examples.source: Returns an unbiased estimate of the expectation value
examples.suggested: Restituisce una stima non distorta del valore di aspettazione
examples.translation: Restituisce una stima imparziale del valore di aspettazione
examples.why: "imparziale" is the moral/fairness sense of unbiased; the statistical term of art in Italian is "non distorta" (or "non polarizzata"). Recognizable but wrong register for an estimator.

examples.source: Directed execution model
examples.suggested: Modello di esecuzione diretta
examples.translation: Modello di esecuzione diretto
examples.why: Agreement puts "diretto" on "modello", so it reads "direct model of execution" rather than "model of directed execution"; the feminine "diretta" attaches the qualifier to "esecuzione" as in the English.

examples.source: Noise-tailoring technique that transforms any noise channel into a Pauli channel
examples.suggested: Tecnica di modellazione del rumore che trasforma qualsiasi canale di rumore in un canale di Pauli
examples.translation: Tecnica di adattamento al rumore che trasforma qualsiasi canale di rumore in un canale di Pauli
examples.why: "adattamento al rumore" says the technique adapts to the noise; "noise tailoring" means it reshapes the noise. The following clause limits the damage, so this is a nuance flattening rather than a misleading claim.

examples.source: Dynamical decoupling / PEC with shaded lightcones
examples.suggested: Disaccoppiamento dinamico (or keep "Dynamical decoupling" whole) / PEC con coni di luce sfumati
examples.translation: Decoupling dinamico / PEC con lightcone sfumati
examples.why: Half-translated compounds: the noun stays English while only the modifier is Italianized. Italian technical writing either keeps the English term intact or translates it fully.

editor_note: Content is faithful throughout — figures, the RSA1024/RSA250 narrative, "teorema fondamentale dell'aritmetica", "algoritmo di Euclide" and MCD terminology are all correct and consistent — but the closing paragraph has the file's real problems. The idiom "but don't hold your breath" is calqued as a conditional statement "ma non tratteneresti il respiro" ("but you wouldn't hold your breath"), which is not Italian and loses the authorial warning; the same sentence's neighbour has a subjunctive error ("Sebbene ci si potrebbe aspettare" instead of "ci si possa aspettare"). Earlier, "an efficient algorithm for integer factoring would break it" is softened to "lo renderebbe vulnerabile" (would make it vulnerable), understating the categorical claim about RSA. Minor translationese elsewhere: "dimostrazioni di codice" for "code demonstrations" and "migliaia di anni-CPU-core" for "thousands of CPU core-years". None of these teach a false concept, so this stays MINOR.

examples.source: One could be discovered tomorrow — but don't hold your breath.
examples.suggested: Potrebbe essere scoperto domani — ma non ci contare troppo.
examples.translation: Potrebbe essere scoperto domani — ma non tratteneresti il respiro.
examples.why: The English idiom is an imperative warning to the reader; the Italian renders it as a literal second-person conditional ('you wouldn't hold your breath'), which is meaningless in Italian and drops the rhetorical caveat that sets up the final sentence.

examples.source: The security of the RSA public-key cryptosystem is based on the computational difficulty of integer factoring, in the sense that an efficient algorithm for integer factoring would break it.
examples.suggested: ...nel senso che un algoritmo efficiente per la fattorizzazione intera lo violerebbe / ne comprometterebbe la sicurezza.
examples.translation: ...nel senso che un algoritmo efficiente per la fattorizzazione intera lo renderebbe vulnerabile.
examples.why: 'break it' is an absolute claim (the cryptosystem is defeated); 'renderebbe vulnerabile' softens it to 'would make it vulnerable', weakening the point the section is built on.

examples.source: Although we might expect that an efficient algorithm for factoring ... would have been discovered by now
examples.suggested: Sebbene ci si possa aspettare che un algoritmo efficiente per la fattorizzazione ... sarebbe già stato scoperto
examples.translation: Sebbene ci si potrebbe aspettare che un algoritmo efficiente per la fattorizzazione ... sarebbe già stato scoperto
examples.why: 'Sebbene' requires the subjunctive; 'ci si potrebbe aspettare' is a grammatical slip a native technical writer would not make, and the very long clause chain reads as machine-ordered English syntax.

examples.source: A few simple code demonstrations in Python ... thousands of CPU core-years
examples.suggested: Alcuni semplici esempi di codice in Python ... migliaia di anni-core di CPU
examples.translation: Alcune semplici dimostrazioni di codice in Python ... migliaia di anni-CPU-core
examples.why: Both are word-order calques: 'dimostrazioni di codice' is not idiomatic Italian for 'code demonstrations', and 'anni-CPU-core' stacks the English compound instead of the Italian 'anni-core di CPU'.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no inverted conditions, no hallucinated claims; the Born-rule paragraph, the |+>/|-> discrimination argument ("possono quindi essere discriminati *perfettamente*"), the square-root-of-NOT passage and the permutation-matrix/stochastic-and-unitary iff statement all land exactly as in the English, and core terminology is correct and consistent (qubit, norma euclidea, vettori unitari, misura nella base standard, matrici unitarie/stocastiche, trasformata di Fourier quantistica, stato più/stato meno). The defects are surface-level: a malformed gerund "la matrice ottenuta traspondo $U$" (should be "trasponendo"), and three calques/translationese a native technical editor would rewrite — "allevia la necessità di specificare" for "alleviates the need", "la stessa distribuzione di output" for "the same output distribution" (Italian would say "degli esiti"/"dei risultati", especially since the file otherwise uses "esiti"), and "Anzi, abbandoneremo…" for "In fact, we'll mostly abandon…" where "Anzi" reads as a contrastive "on the contrary" rather than a confirming "in effetti". Informal "tu" register holds cleanly (Nota, tieni presente, Immagina).

examples.source: meaning the matrix obtained by transposing $U$ and taking the complex conjugate of each entry.
examples.suggested: ovvero la matrice ottenuta trasponendo $U$ e prendendo il complesso coniugato di ogni componente.
examples.translation: ovvero la matrice ottenuta traspondo $U$ e prendendo il complesso coniugato di ogni componente.
examples.why: "traspondo" is not a valid form — the gerund of "trasporre" is "trasponendo". Grammatical slip, meaning still recoverable.

examples.source: it alleviates the need to explicitly specify an ordering of the classical states
examples.suggested: evita la necessità di specificare esplicitamente un ordinamento degli stati classici
examples.translation: allevia la necessità di specificare esplicitamente un ordinamento degli stati classici
examples.why: "alleviare la necessità" is a direct calque of "alleviate the need"; Italian technical prose uses "evita/elimina la necessità".

examples.source: Measuring either state produces the same output distribution as the other
examples.suggested: Misurare uno dei due stati produce la stessa distribuzione degli esiti dell'altro
examples.translation: Misurare uno qualsiasi dei due stati produce la stessa distribuzione di output dell'altro
examples.why: "distribuzione di output" is an anglicism inconsistent with the file's own "esiti" (used for "outcomes" throughout the measurement section).

examples.source: In fact, we'll mostly abandon the column vector representation of state vectors
examples.suggested: In effetti, abbandoneremo quasi completamente la rappresentazione mediante vettori colonna dei vettori di stato
examples.translation: Anzi, abbandoneremo quasi completamente la rappresentazione mediante vettori colonna degli stati
examples.why: "Anzi" carries a contrastive/corrective force the English "In fact" does not have here; "In effetti"/"Di fatto" preserves the confirming tone. The head noun "vettori di stato" is also reduced to "stati".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no inversion, no hallucination: the open-source caveat keeps both polarities correct (サービス・ソフトウェアは**オープンソースではありません** vs クライアント…は**オープンソース**です), the Open Plan restriction (オープン・プランのユーザーは Session ジョブを送信できません) is preserved, and domain terms are right and consistent (ショット数, プリミティブ, オブザーバブル, トランスパイル, エラー抑制/エラー緩和, ゼロノイズ外挿). Three editor-level nits remain: (1) the mandated informal register slips into keigo once — "GitHub 組織をご覧ください" for "visit our GitHub organization" (should be 参照してください, as used everywhere else in the file); (2) the three execution modes are rendered inconsistently inside one enumeration — "ジョブ、Session、バッチ" translates Job and Batch but keeps Session in English, and the same split continues in the following sentences (ジョブは… / Session を使用すると… / バッチ・モードでは…); (3) "domain-familiar inputs and outputs" is flattened to "ドメイン固有の入出力" (domain-specific), losing the "familiar to the domain expert" nuance that is the point of the sentence. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: To get involved with Qiskit open-source efforts, visit our GitHub organization at github.com/Qiskit
examples.suggested: … GitHub 組織を参照してください。
examples.translation: Qiskit のオープンソース活動に参加するには、[github.com/Qiskit] … にある GitHub 組織をご覧ください。
examples.why: ご覧ください is keigo; the file's convention is plain desu/masu with 参照してください (used for the docs/installation/setup links elsewhere in the same file).

examples.source: three types of execution modes …: Job, Session, and Batch
examples.suggested: ジョブ、セッション、バッチ（or keep all three in English: Job、Session、Batch）
examples.translation: 3 種類の実行モードも含まれています：[ジョブ、Session、バッチ]
examples.why: Two of the three mode names are localized and the third is left in English inside one list, and the split persists in the explanatory sentences that follow (ジョブは… / Session を使用すると… / バッチ・モードでは…). Recognizable, but an editor would make the trio uniform.

examples.source: Users can prototype industry applications with domain-familiar inputs and outputs.
examples.suggested: ユーザーは自分のドメインで使い慣れた入出力を使って、業界アプリケーションのプロトタイプを作成できます。
examples.translation: ユーザーはドメイン固有の入出力で業界アプリケーションのプロトタイプを作成できます。
examples.why: 'domain-familiar' is about inputs the domain expert already knows how to work with; ドメイン固有 says 'domain-specific', which shifts the selling point from user familiarity to technical specialization. Minor nuance loss, not a false statement.

editor_note: Faithful overall, correct です/ます register with no keigo, and the Scope paragraph's restructuring of the "representing a project ... including using an official e-mail address" chain into a parenthetical reads natively. Four editorial slips: (1) in the unacceptable-behavior list "sexual attention" is rendered 性的な注意, where 注意 means "caution/warning" — the intended sense is 性的な関心の押し付け; (2) step 2 of the reporting procedure drops the alternative trigger "or correct the issue", leaving only 本人がすぐに行動を停止しない場合; (3) "If you feel comfortable" in step 1 becomes 可能であれば ("if possible"), shifting the condition from the reporter's emotional comfort to feasibility; (4) "respect and dignity" becomes 尊重と敬意 ("respect and esteem") rather than 尊重と尊厳. None of these teaches a false rule, but each is something a native technical editor would change.

examples.source: unwelcome physical contact, sexual attention, or advances
examples.suggested: 望まれない身体的接触、性的な関心の押し付け、または言い寄り
examples.translation: 望まれない身体的接触、性的な注意、またはアプローチ
examples.why: 性的な注意 is a calque: 注意 in Japanese reads as "caution/warning/care", not "attention directed at someone", so the item in a harassment list is momentarily confusing.

examples.source: If the person does not immediately stop the behavior or correct the issue, or if you're uncomfortable speaking up, flag a moderator
examples.suggested: 本人がすぐに行動をやめない、または問題を是正しない場合、あるいは指摘しづらい場合は、モデレーターに報告し
examples.translation: 本人がすぐに行動を停止しない場合、または発言しづらい場合は、モデレーターに報告し
examples.why: The alternative trigger "or correct the issue" is dropped, narrowing the conditions under which the reader is told to escalate to a moderator.

examples.source: If you feel comfortable, let the person know that what they did is not appropriate
examples.suggested: 差し支えなければ、その行為が不適切であることを本人に伝え
examples.translation: 可能であれば、その行為が不適切であることを本人に伝え
examples.why: 可能であれば means "if possible" (feasibility); the English condition is whether the reader feels personally comfortable confronting the person, an important nuance in a reporting procedure.

examples.source: treating every individual with respect and dignity
examples.suggested: すべての個人を尊重と尊厳をもって扱う
examples.translation: すべての個人を尊重と敬意をもって扱う
examples.why: "dignity" is 尊厳; 敬意 ("esteem/deference") makes the pair near-synonymous with 尊重 and flattens the pledge.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the technical numbers (400 分, 120 qubit, トランスパイルされた 2-Qubit 深度が約 30 前後, 30〜120 分, 約 10 倍改善されたエラー率) and the caveats ("これは高速な汎用コンピューターではありません", "文字通りのエラー緩和戦略", Quantum Credits が「学生や広範な量子コミュニティのメンバーは利用できません」) all survive intact, so nothing here misleads a learner. What a native technical editor would change: (a) "calls" (funding solicitations / 公募) is rendered as 申請 / 申請書 in four places — 「申請例/注記」, 「Basic Energy Sciences 量子申請」, 「資金提供機関の申請書に直接アクセス」, 「DOE の量子 R&D 申請」 — which flips the direction (agency's call vs applicant's application), while the very same sentence at l.142 correctly uses 公募, so the file is internally inconsistent; (b) two genuinely ungrammatical/calqued spots: 「成熟するにつれた地域イノベーション・エコシステムの刺激」 (l.176) and the dangling 「明確にしておきたいのは、IBM Quantum は…お伝えできるわけではありません」 (l.12, missing ということです); (c) 「量子後暗号」 for post-quantum cryptography is a literal calque where the field says 耐量子計算機暗号 / ポスト量子暗号 (likewise 量子安全な for quantum-safe), and research "controls" is rendered 管理 rather than 対照; (d) light keigo slips against the informal convention (ご存じ ×2, お伝えできる, お住まいの地域, お勧めします). None of these change what the page teaches.

examples.source: Example calls/notes … Basic Energy Sciences quantum calls … we recommend going directly to funding agency calls … active solicitations like DOE's quantum R&D calls
examples.suggested: 公募例/注記 … Basic Energy Sciences の量子公募 … 資金提供機関の公募情報を直接確認する … DOE の量子 R&D 公募
examples.translation: 申請例/注記 … Basic Energy Sciences 量子申請 … 資金提供機関の申請書に直接アクセスする … DOE の量子 R&D 申請などのアクティブな公募
examples.why: "call" here is the agency's funding solicitation (公募), not the applicant's 申請/申請書; the rendering reverses who issues the document, and 公募 is used correctly in the same sentence at l.142, so the file contradicts itself.

examples.source: stimulating regional innovation ecosystems as quantum technologies mature into deployable tools for science and industry
examples.suggested: 量子技術が科学と産業で実用可能なツールへと成熟するにつれて地域のイノベーション・エコシステムを活性化すること
examples.translation: 量子技術が科学と産業の展開可能なツールへと成熟するにつれた地域イノベーション・エコシステムの刺激
examples.why: 「〜するにつれた」は日本語として非文。名詞化した「刺激」も硬く、ネイティブの技術ライターは書かない形。

examples.source: quantum‑safe cybersecurity skills for migration to post-quantum cryptography
examples.suggested: 耐量子計算機暗号（ポスト量子暗号）への移行に向けた耐量子サイバーセキュリティのスキル
examples.translation: 量子後暗号への移行のための量子安全なサイバーセキュリティスキル
examples.why: post-quantum cryptography の定訳は耐量子計算機暗号／ポスト量子暗号。「量子後暗号」「量子安全な」は逐語的な造語で、意味は推測できるものの分野の用語ではない。

examples.source: Address rigor and reproducibility including data quality, controls, analysis and sharing.
examples.suggested: データ品質、対照（コントロール）、分析、共有を含む厳密性と再現性に対応します。
examples.translation: データ品質、管理、分析、および共有を含む厳密さと再現性に対処します。
examples.why: 研究提案の文脈の controls は実験の「対照」であり「管理」ではない。取り違えても致命的ではないが、専門読者には別概念に読める。

examples.source: you likely know how to write grants very well / IBM Quantum cannot tell you / we recommend going directly to…
examples.suggested: よく知っていると思います／お近くの地域に（もしくは単に「地域に」）／推奨します
examples.translation: よくご存じのことと思います／お住まいの地域に／お勧めします
examples.why: 本コースの規約は敬語なしの丁寧体。ご存じ・お伝え・お住まい・お勧め は軽度の敬語で、数箇所のみのため軽微だが統一されていない。

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout: the tip about Serverless "getting an upgrade / features changing fast" (アップグレード中であり、その機能は急速に変化しています), the saved-credentials precondition (認証情報が保存済みであることを前提としています) with its "if you have not" branch, and the Next-steps paper description (量子中心のスーパーコンピューティング / 量子化学の探求) all match the English with no drift, dropped caveat, or invented claim. The one thing a native technical editor would change is a honorific-register slip in the tip admonition: 「ページでリリースノートと最新ドキュメントをご確認ください」 uses the ご〜ください form the house style excludes, and it also turns the English's plain statement of where to find things ("find release notes and the most recent documentation at ... page") into a directive; plain 確認できます / 掲載されています would fit both the register convention and the source. Everything else — 実験のアップデート for "Update the experiment", the ローカル実験 tab label, 出力 for "Output" — is defensible and consistent.

examples.source: During this development phase, find release notes and the most recent documentation at the Qiskit Serverless GitHub page.
examples.suggested: この開発フェーズ中は、[Qiskit Serverless GitHub] ページでリリースノートと最新ドキュメントを確認できます。
examples.translation: この開発フェーズ中は、[Qiskit Serverless GitHub] ページでリリースノートと最新ドキュメントをご確認ください。
examples.why: ご確認ください is the ご〜ください honorific pattern the file's desu/masu-without-keigo convention excludes (same class as ご覧ください), and it converts the English's neutral 'you can find X at Y' into an instruction. Not misleading, but a register slip a native technical editor would rewrite.

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout — every conditional (β=0→θ=0 with φ arbitrary; α=0→θ=π; neither zero→unique (θ,φ)), every coordinate pair ((0,0,1)/(1,0,φ), (1,0,0)/(1,π/2,0), (0,-1,0)/(1,π/2,3π/2)), the antipodal-pair caveat and the Bloch-ball/mixed-state distinction all survive intact, and terminology is correct and consistent (密度行列, パウリ行列, 純粋状態, 完全混合状態, 極角/方位角, 対蹠点, グローバル位相). What a native technical editor would change is phrasing: the coined compound「ブロッホ球点」(heading 「ブロッホ球点の凸結合」and again at line ~239) reads as an unnatural noun-stack where Japanese wants「ブロッホ球上の点」; 「後ほど事柄を単純にするためです」is a word-for-word calque of "make things simpler a bit later on"; and 「北極から南に向かって記述する点に到達するまでの回転角」leaves 「記述する点」ambiguous (parses as "the point that describes") where the English means "the point being described". None of these mislead — meaning and pedagogy are preserved — so they are stylistic MINORs only. Register is consistent desu/masu with no keigo.

examples.source: ## Convex combinations of points … A different example concerning convex combinations of Bloch sphere points is the one discussed in the previous subsection.
examples.suggested: ## ブロッホ球上の点の凸結合 … ブロッホ球上の点の凸結合に関する別の例として、…
examples.translation: ## ブロッホ球点の凸結合 … ブロッホ球点の凸結合に関する別の例として、前の小節で論じたものがあります。
examples.why: 「ブロッホ球点」is a coined noun-stack that no Japanese technical writer would use; the idiomatic form is「ブロッホ球上の点」, which the same file already uses correctly at line 209 (「ブロッホ球上の点の凸結合を取ることで」) — so the file is also internally inconsistent about it.

examples.source: …because this is a conventional way to parameterize vectors of this sort, and it will make things simpler a bit later on.
examples.suggested: …この種のベクトルをパラメータ化する慣例的な方法であり、後で話が少し簡単になるからです。
examples.translation: …この種のベクトルをパラメータ化する慣例的な方法であり、後ほど事柄を単純にするためです。
examples.why: 「事柄を単純にする」is a literal calque of "make things simpler";「事柄」is not used this way in Japanese expository prose. Meaning is intact, but the sentence reads as MT.

examples.source: the polar angle θ is how far we rotate south from the north pole to reach the point being described
examples.suggested: 極角 $\theta$ は、北極から南に向かって、対象とする点に到達するまでに回転する角度であり
examples.translation: 極角 $\theta$ は北極から南に向かって記述する点に到達するまでの回転角であり
examples.why: 「記述する点」most naturally parses as "the point that describes (something)" rather than the intended "the point being described"; a reader must back-track. The geometric content is still recoverable, so this is stiffness rather than drift.

editor_note: No misleading content: every substantive claim (Cliffordization preserves structure/depth, to_clifford does not mutate two-qubit gates/qubit count/depth, the 90%/90%/80% mitigation thresholds and their direction, "all differences are below 90% so PEA should help") is faithfully carried over, and the register is consistent desu/masu with no keigo. What a native technical editor would still change: (1) the three guideline bullets uniformly weaken English's "will likely not help" / "will likely be able to improve" to the flat 可能性があります, dropping the probability qualifier (direction is preserved, so this reads as a lost nuance rather than a reversal); (2) core-term rendering is split within the file — 6量子ビット回路 (line 80) vs 対象Circuit / クリフォードCircuit elsewhere, and within one sentence 非クリフォード単一Qubit Gate next to 2 qubit Gate、Qubit数 (line 160); (3) headings calque English as アプリケーション1／アプリケーション2 where a Japanese author would write 応用例; (4) 期待値を設定する for "set up expectations" (line 186) is an unfortunate false friend in an Estimator guide where 期待値 means expectation value; (5) the closing sentence of Application 1 (line 331) misplaces the parenthetical so it reads as "the noise impact of the (Cliffordized version of the) target PUB", which is clumsy though still parseable.

examples.source: If the mean absolute difference is greater than 90%, mitigation will likely not help. ... PEA will likely be able to improve the results.
examples.suggested: 平均絶対差が90%を超える場合、エラー緩和では改善が見込めない可能性が高いです。…PEAによって結果が改善される可能性が高いです。
examples.translation: 平均絶対差が90%を超える場合、エラー緩和は効果がない可能性があります。…[PEA]によって結果が改善される可能性があります。
examples.why: English states a likelihood ("will likely not help" / "will likely be able to improve"); the Japanese flattens all three bullets to the neutral 可能性があります, dropping the qualifier. The direction of the advice is unchanged, so this does not mislead, but the confidence the guideline conveys is lost.

examples.source: Consider a six-qubit circuit ... non-Clifford single-qubit gates ... two-qubit gates, number of qubits
examples.suggested: Pick one convention per term: either 量子ビット/回路 throughout, or Qubit/Circuit throughout; and render two-qubit gates the same way as single-qubit gates (2 Qubit Gate).
examples.translation: 6量子ビット回路を考えます／対象Circuitの初期化／非クリフォード単一Qubit Gate…2 qubit Gate、Qubit数
examples.why: Within-file split of the two most frequent domain terms — 量子ビット vs Qubit and 回路 vs Circuit — plus a lowercase, space-separated '2 qubit Gate' sitting beside '単一Qubit Gate' in the same sentence. The concept stays identifiable, so this is a consistency slip, not a comprehension failure.

examples.source: ## Application 1: Analyze the impact of noise on the circuit outputs / ## Application 2: Benchmark different strategies
examples.suggested: ## 応用例1：Circuit出力に対するノイズの影響を分析する / ## 応用例2：異なる戦略をベンチマークする
examples.translation: ## アプリケーション1：Circuit出力に対するノイズの影響を分析する / ## アプリケーション2：異なる戦略をベンチマークする
examples.why: アプリケーション in Japanese technical prose normally means an application program; for 'Application N' as a worked use case, 応用例 is what a Japanese-writing engineer would use. Reads as a calque of the English heading.

examples.source: This can be useful to set up expectations on the quality of the experimental results before running a job on a QPU.
examples.suggested: これは、QPU上でジョブを実行する前に実験結果の品質をどの程度見込めるかを把握するのに役立ちます。
examples.translation: これは、QPU上でジョブを実行する前に実験結果の品質に対する期待値を設定するのに役立ちます。
examples.why: 期待値 is the established term for 'expectation value' — the very quantity this Estimator-focused guide computes — so using it for the everyday sense of 'expectations' invites a momentary misread. Not wrong Japanese, but a poor choice in this specific document.

examples.source: you can try to quantify the impact of noise on the (Cliffordized version of the) PUBs of interest before running them on a QPU
examples.suggested: QPU上で実行する前に、対象のPUB（のクリフォード化バージョン）に対するノイズの影響を定量化できます
examples.translation: 対象のPUBの（クリフォード化バージョンの）ノイズの影響をQPU上で実行する前に定量化しようとすることができます
examples.why: The parenthetical is spliced between 対象のPUBの and ノイズの影響, so the phrase parses as '(the Cliffordized version's) noise impact of the target PUB'; combined with 定量化しようとすることができます it is a stiff word-for-word tracking of the English clause order.

editor_note: Faithful and natural throughout; both polarity-critical admonitions survive intact (「測定を含めては**なりません**」 for Estimator vs 「必ず測定を含める**必要があります**」 for Sampler), and core terms are correct and consistent (observable→オブザーバブル, expectation value→期待値, statevector→状態ベクトル, quasi-probability distribution→準確率分布, bitstrings→ビット列, transpile→トランスパイル, classical register→古典レジスタ), with the `precision`/shot-noise caveat 「`.run()` メソッド内でのみ定義されます」 preserved exactly.

No semantic drift: the whole prose body (PUB definition, error-mitigation overhead paragraph, both "Inicializar a conta" sections, "valor esperado" for expectation value) matches the English claim for claim, and the informal "você" register holds throughout. Two editorial slips: (1) IBM's product plan name "Open Plan" is rendered as "Plano Gratuito" in the Próximos passos admonition — descriptively true but it renames a plan the learner must find by name in the console, and it clashes with the rest of the pt corpus, which uses "Open Plan" (run-jobs-session.mdx, plans-overview.mdx, instances.mdx) or "Plano Aberto" (v2-primitives.mdx, sampler-rest-api.mdx). (2) The three "Learn how to…" bullets are calqued as "Aprenda como trabalhar / Aprenda como inicializar / Aprenda como transpilar"; a native technical writer would use "Saiba como…" — "aprenda como" reads as English syntax carried over. Neither misleads.

examples.source: Note that Open Plan users cannot submit session jobs.
examples.suggested: Observe que usuários do Open Plan não podem enviar jobs de sessão.
examples.translation: Observe que usuários do Plano Gratuito não podem submeter jobs em sessão.
examples.why: "Open Plan" is an IBM product name shown untranslated in the Platform UI; the rest of the pt corpus keeps "Open Plan" or uses "Plano Aberto", so "Plano Gratuito" is an ad-hoc third rendering the learner cannot map to the console.

examples.source: Learn how to initialize your account … Learn how to transpile locally …
examples.suggested: Saiba como [inicializar sua conta] … Saiba como transpilar localmente na seção [Transpile].
examples.translation: Aprenda como [inicializar sua conta] … Aprenda como transpilar localmente na seção [Transpile].
examples.why: "Aprenda como + infinitive" is a direct calque of "Learn how to"; Brazilian technical docs use "Saiba como" (or "Aprenda a"), so the three bullets read as machine-rendered English.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and the pedagogy survives intact: the SPMD/rank explanation, the "não necessariamente um 'rank' no sentido de priorização" caveat, the non-parallelizable SQD sequence, and the Estimator/Sampler check-your-understanding answers all match the source, and core terms are correct and consistent (transpilação, portas nativas, valor esperado de um observável, estados da base computacional, escalonador, grafo acíclico dirigido). Two small lexical slips a native technical editor would still fix. In the "Programação paralela" section, "multi-node supercomputing" becomes "computação de alto desempenho em múltiplos nós", conflating supercomputação with the course's own distinct HPC term (the lesson sits inside the "high-performance computing" course), and in the same clause "heterogeneous quantum-classical jobs" becomes "jobs híbridos quântico-clássicos" — an inconsistency, since "heterogeneous" is rendered "heterogêneo/heterogênea" everywhere else in the file (ambientes heterogêneos, infraestrutura de computação heterogênea, computação heterogênea). Neither misleads a learner; both are within-file consistency/word-choice fixes.

examples.source: Here, we'll focus on the distributed memory model because it is essential for multi-node supercomputing and coordinating large-scale heterogeneous quantum-classical jobs.
examples.suggested: ... porque ele é essencial para a supercomputação em múltiplos nós e para coordenar jobs heterogêneos quântico-clássicos em larga escala.
examples.translation: Aqui, vamos nos concentrar no modelo de memória distribuída porque ele é essencial para a computação de alto desempenho em múltiplos nós e para coordenar jobs híbridos quântico-clássicos em larga escala.
examples.why: 'supercomputing' is flattened into 'computação de alto desempenho' (HPC), which is the course's own separate term, and 'heterogeneous' is swapped for 'híbridos' even though 'heterogêneo' is the rendering used consistently everywhere else in this file (ambientes heterogêneos, infraestrutura de computação heterogênea). Not misleading, but it blurs two terms the lesson keeps distinct.

examples.source: A model histogram of results from sampler. Some states are very likely to be measured, others are very unlikely.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked the drift-prone claims (SWAP = três portas CNOT, Toffoli "até seis portas CNOT", NP-difícil, "usado apenas nos níveis de otimização 1, 2 e 3 quando um layout perfeito não é encontrado", "só é executado se for explicitamente solicitado ... e não é executado por padrão") and every condition, quantity and caveat matches the English; no hallucinated sentence appears. Two editorial slips: the core transpiler term "pass" is split within the file — "a heuristic pass" becomes "um passo heurístico" (line ~56, colliding with "dois passos"/"este primeiro passo" used for "steps" in the very same sentence) while everywhere else it is "passe"/"passes"; and the adverb "Tipicamente" is calqued from "Typically" five times ("Tipicamente, isso envolve", "tipicamente usados", "tipicamente calculado", "tipicamente leva", "é tipicamente usado"), which a Portuguese technical writer would vary with "Normalmente"/"Em geral". One further stiffness: "Para obter algum entendimento" for "To gain some insight". None of these mislead; terminology otherwise correct and consistent (qubit, porta, profundidade, roteamento, mapeador SWAP, transpilação, estado GHZ) and the informal "você" register holds.

Within-file split of a core term.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every instruction, caveat and negation is faithfully carried over (the "você **não pode** usar `pip install -U qiskit`" warning, "apenas plataformas de 64 bits são suportadas", "não é testado e você terá que compilar ... a partir do código-fonte" all match the English exactly), and the informal "você" register holds throughout. (2) Two calques read as MT rather than native technical Portuguese: "permitirão atualizações no local" for "in-place upgrades" (also stacking "Atualizações futuras ... permitirão atualizações"), and "O suporte para esses sistemas operacionais é de melhor esforço apenas." with English word order for "best effort only". editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no hallucinated claims; the AQC narrative (estado alvo → ansatz com menos etapas de Trotter → aproximado iterativamente → combinado com o restante das etapas de Trotter) and the dry-run/validation paragraphs all track the English exactly, and core terms are consistent (Hamiltoniano, valores esperados, observável, ansatz, transpilado, fidelidade de parada). What a native technical editor would still change: (1) "usando declarações print" in the logging paragraph is a calque of "print statements" — in PT "declaração" means a declaration, not a statement; "instruções/comandos print" is the idiomatic rendering. (3) "executado em um QPU" uses masculine agreement where PT convention treats QPU (unidade de processamento quântico) as feminine ("em uma QPU"). None of these mislead a learner; they are style/agreement slips only.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversions, no swapped quantities, no hallucinations; the LWE/BDD/CVP definitions, the Regev security argument, the Module-LWE "meio-termo entre LWE e Ring-LWE" trade-off and the IND-CPA/IND-CCA discussion all track the English exactly, and the translation even repairs the broken English grammar of the Hybrid-cryptography opener. Four things a native editor would fix: (1) the closing summary sentence of the English ("As we navigate the complex landscape … in the quantum era.") is simply absent — the PT file ends at the CRYSTALS paragraph; (2) the `DefinitionTooltip` definition for *reticulados modulares* is left entirely in English ("Collection of all submodules of a given module…"), so a PT reader hovering that term gets English prose; (3) "quantum-safe" is rendered three ways in the same file — "criptografia quântica segura" (headings/intro), "algoritmos quânticos seguros" (bullet list) and "quântico-seguro" (liboqs/KEM/summary sections); (4) two stiff calques: "Os criptologistas quânticos seguros" for "Quantum-safe cryptologists", and "um reticulado inteiro dado" for "a given integer lattice", which in PT reads more naturally as "the whole lattice" than as "integer lattice".

O conjunto de todos os submódulos forma um reticulado, isto é, um conjunto parcialmente ordenado no qual dois elementos quaisquer têm supremo e ínfimo únicos."

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the cost/latency claims, the "até cinco jobs clássicos ... em paralelo" quantity, the "menos de um minuto de tempo de QPU" threshold, the variational-loop steps and the noise-model caveat ("pode ficar desatualizado quando o próximo job sair da fila") all match the English exactly, and the informal "você" register holds throughout. Three editorial slips: (1) the Job bullet "Pode ser executado antes do modo batch" reads as sequencing ("executed before batch mode") rather than the intended comparative "pode começar a ser executado mais cedo do que no modo batch"; (2) "which makes them more flexible to work with" (the jobs) is generalized to "o que torna o processo mais flexível", shifting the referent from the individual jobs to the workflow; (3) "wall-clock time" is handled two ways in the same file — left in English in "a duração do experimento (wall-clock time)" but calqued as "o tempo de relógio de parede (wall-clock time)" a few paragraphs earlier. None of these would teach a learner something false.

examples.translation: Pode ser executado antes do modo batch.
examples.why: "antes do modo batch" reads as temporal sequencing (job runs, then batch runs) instead of the English comparative "sooner than [it would in] batch mode". A native technical writer would use "mais cedo do que" to keep it a comparison of start times.

examples.translation: poderá obter resultados de jobs individuais, o que torna o processo mais flexível
examples.why: The English "them" refers to the individual jobs; the translation reassigns the flexibility to "o processo" (the workflow). Meaning is not falsified, but the specific pedagogical point — that partitioned jobs are individually manipulable — is blurred.

examples.source: wall-clock time (used twice)

editor_note: The prose is generally fluent and the core terminology is sound and consistent (superposição, entrelaçamento, interferência, qubit, portas lógicas, estados puros, probabilismo clássico), but the "Verifique seu entendimento" answer in the Quantum circuits section rewrites a factual definition: the English "a software development kit (SDK) like [Qiskit]" becomes "uma linguagem de programação como o [Qiskit]", teaching the learner the false concept that Qiskit is a programming language rather than an SDK — in a module whose stated objective is recognizing exactly these distinctions. The same sentence also silently renames "IBM Quantum Composer" to "o Composer da IBM". Secondary, non-misleading slips: the ungrammatical "se limitava ao escala de cinza" (should be "à escala de cinza"), the non-Portuguese calque "por quanto você sabe" for "as far as you know" (should be "até onde você sabe"), and "a fotografia pré-colorida" for "pre-color film photography", which reads as "pre-colored photography". The coin abbreviations cara (C) / coroa (K) are an odd but internally consistent choice and are not a defect.

examples.source: We can use a visual tool like [IBM Quantum Composer](...) or a software development kit (SDK) like [Qiskit](...) to construct quantum circuits.

examples.translation: Podemos usar uma ferramenta visual como o [Composer](...) da IBM ou uma linguagem de programação como o [Qiskit](...) para construir circuitos quânticos.
examples.why: Qiskit is an SDK (a Python library), not a programming language. The translation drops the source's explicit SDK definition and asserts something factually false, so a learner finishes the module with a wrong mental model of what Qiskit is. The product name 'IBM Quantum Composer' is also altered to 'o Composer da IBM'.

examples.source: ...but not looked at the outcome, as far as you know each coin might be heads or tails.

examples.why: 'por quanto você sabe' is a literal word-for-word calque of 'as far as you know' that does not exist in Portuguese; the idiom is 'até onde você sabe' / 'pelo que você sabe'.

examples.source: The physical phenomena of color existed while photography was limited to grayscale.

examples.why: Gender/contraction error: 'escala' is feminine, so it must be 'à escala de cinza', not 'ao escala'. A native technical editor would never leave this.

examples.why: 'fotografia pré-colorida' reads as 'pre-colored photography' (a photograph that was colored beforehand) rather than 'photography before color film'; the historical framing of the analogy is blurred.

editor_note: Meaning is preserved throughout — the credentials caveat, the cloud-setup link, the API-key authentication step and the "Follow the instructions on the Introduction to Qiskit Functions page" sentence all land correctly, and register is consistently informal. Three surface problems a native technical editor would fix: (1) the tip admonition renders "is getting an upgrade" as the malformed verb "nagbe-bago" (correct reduplication is "nagbabago"/"nag-a-upgrade"), which both reads as broken Tagalog and flattens "upgrade" into plain "change", making the sentence redundant with the following "mabilis na nagbabago ang mga feature nito"; (2) the same admonition uses "mahanap ang mga release notes" where an imperative is required — a native writer writes "hanapin ang…", not the infinitive/ability form "mahanap"; (3) "Read a paper" becomes "Basahin ang isang papel", a calque — bare "papel" in Tagalog means a sheet of paper or a role, so "papel-pananaliksik"/"artikulo" is needed for an academic paper. None of these teaches a false concept, so this stays MINOR.

examples.translation: **Ang Qiskit Serverless ay nagbe-bago, at mabilis na nagbabago ang mga feature nito.**
examples.why: "nagbe-bago" is not a well-formed Tagalog verb (the correct reduplicated form is "nagbabago"), and rendering "getting an upgrade" as generic "changing" makes the clause redundant with the second half of the same sentence.

examples.why: The English is an instruction to the reader; "mahanap" is the infinitive/ability form and reads as broken instruction-giving. Tagalog imperative here is "hanapin".

examples.translation: Basahin ang isang papel kung saan gumamit ang mga mananaliksik ng Qiskit Serverless…
examples.why: Bare "papel" in Tagalog means a physical sheet of paper or a role, not an academic publication; this is a direct calque of English "paper".

editor_note: No inversion, hallucination or quantity swap survived the paragraph-by-paragraph read — the Eastin-Knill statement, the distiller "if any outcome is 1 the process failed / if every outcome is 0 the state is less noisy" logic, the weight-3 Shor-code Pauli example and the S/T magic-state branch outcomes are all faithful. What a native technical editor would change: (1) "non-destructively" (measuring stabilizer generators via phase estimation) is rendered "nang hindi mapanganib" = "without being dangerous", which is the wrong property — it should be "nang hindi sinisira ang state"; (2) "an $X$ error occurring on *both* qubits" becomes "sa *parehong* qubit", which a Tagalog reader can just as easily parse as "on the SAME qubit" (the next paragraph's "ginagawang dalawang error" is what rescues it) — "sa magkabilang qubit"/"sa dalawang qubit" would be unambiguous; (3) "propagate errors to a workspace system" uses "pinalalapag", an odd/malformed verb inconsistent with the file's own established "kumalat / magkalat / pagkalat" family. There is also a cluster of malformed words that read as sloppy output rather than native writing: "napakahalgang" (napakahalagang), "malulubos" (for "overwhelmed"), "magpalat" (magpakalat), "bawisa" (bawat isa), "medyo ng aksidente" (medyo nagkataon), and "nagpapailalim sa paggamit" for "necessitates the use of". Register is correctly casual throughout (no po/opo).

examples.source: the type of circuit described in "The stabilizer formalism" lesson for measuring stabilizer generators non-destructively using phase estimation
examples.suggested: ...para sa pagsukat ng mga stabilizer generator nang hindi sinisira ang state (non-destructive) gamit ang phase estimation
examples.translation: ang uri ng circuit na inilarawan sa aralin na "The stabilizer formalism" para sa pagsukat ng mga stabilizer generator nang hindi mapanganib gamit ang phase estimation
examples.why: "mapanganib" means dangerous/hazardous. Non-destructive measurement means the encoded state is not collapsed/destroyed; the rendering replaces the defining technical property with an unrelated one, and nothing in the surrounding text repairs it.

examples.source: this is equivalent to an $X$ error occurring on *both* qubits after the controlled-NOT is performed
examples.suggested: ...na nangyayari sa *magkabilang* qubit pagkatapos isagawa ang controlled-NOT
examples.translation: ito ay katumbas ng isang $X$ error na nangyayari sa *parehong* qubit pagkatapos isagawa ang controlled-NOT
examples.why: "parehong" is used later in this same file for "the SAME code block" (line ~116), so here it reads ambiguously as "on the same qubit" — the opposite of the point being taught (one error becoming two). Only the following paragraph's "ginagawang dalawang error" disambiguates it.

examples.source: but instead we *intentionally* propagate errors to a workspace system

examples.translation: ngunit sa halip ay *sadya nating* pinalalapag ang mga error sa isang workspace system

examples.translation: ang ating mga pagsisikap sa error correction ay mabilis na malulubos ng mga error

Together with "magpalat" (line ~28), "bawisa" (line ~47) and "medyo ng aksidente" (line ~241) these read as machine output a native writer would not produce.

editor_note: No semantic drift: the tricky conditionals in the Flex/Premium sections ("limited" vs not limited, active workloads keep running / pending ones stay queued), the Open Plan "10 minuto bawat 28-araw na rolling window", and the v0.40.1 / v0.42 version caveats all match the English exactly, and register stays casual (no po/opo). What a native editor would fix is lexical: "pending" is rendered four times (lines 41, 50, 114, 133) as "nakabinta"/"nakabintang", which is not the Tagalog word for pending — the correct form is "nakabinbin" ("bintang" means accusation) — so "mga nakabintang workload" reads as an error rather than a term. There is also a typo "nagpapapakita" for "nagpapakita" (line 23), the ungrammatical "sa ito" for "dito" (line 109), "maaaring gamitin ang oras" where the actor-focus "maaaring gumamit ng oras" is required (line 111), and "Makipagtulungan sa mga access group" (line 155) for "Work with access groups", which reads as "collaborate with" the groups rather than "use/handle" them.

examples.translation: ngunit ang mga nakabintang workload ay mananatili sa queue hanggang sa may magamit na mas maraming oras
examples.why: "nakabinbin" is the Tagalog term for pending/on hold; "nakabintang" is a different root (bintang = accusation) and reads as a misspelling everywhere "pending" appears, including the admonition title "Mga nakabintang workload".

examples.source: the Instance page shows total usage prior to the current timestamp

examples.suggested: - [Paggamit ng mga access group](/guides/access-groups).
examples.translation: - [Makipagtulungan sa mga access group](/guides/access-groups).
